name: Sonny’s Pizza

name: AleSmith Brewing Company
notes: First-party tasting-room draft menu, two PNG pages linked from alesmith.com/draft-menu/, dated 9/3/26 (transcribed by reading the images - no OCR/text layer). Most beers are priced per pour size under a section-level tier (e.g. "4 OZ. $3 | 8 OZ. $5 | 16 OZ. $8 | 64 OZ. PITCHER $28") that explicitly applies to every beer listed in that section; filed each size as its own line item rather than picking one. AleSmith does not serve its own food - it hosts rotating third-party food trucks onsite (confirmed via alesmith.com FAQ) - so only the brewery's own snacks/drinks are filed; food-truck fare is a different, non-fixed vendor and out of scope.

name: Frida’s Taqueria Oceanside
blocked: partial: restaurant's own site (eatsfridastaqueria.com/menu/) is an empty WordPress/Elementor shell with no menu content, image, or PDF. Uber Eats store page (address confirmed: 2011 Mission Avenue, Oceanside) embeds a __REACT_QUERY_STATE__ payload, but the only catalogItems reachable there are 20 items under Drinks/Mains/Extras/Sides (agua mineral, nachos, quesadilla, salsas, sides) - it is missing the taqueria's core Tacos and Burritos sections entirely, which a live Google snippet for the same store shows priced ($17.31 burrito, $4.25 tacos, $18.47 fries, $14.94 flour quesadillas) but which do not appear in the fetched payload, so the capture is a partial front-end slice, not the full catalog. Cent endings in the captured items are scattered (.44/.87/.64/.59/.39/.73/.01/.43/.33/.49/.89) with no clean divisor found, so a markup on top cannot be ruled out either. Blocking rather than filing a partial catalog missing its core dishes.

name: Ascend Coffee Roasters
blocked:
needs-browser: two first-party ordering surfaces checked, neither yields priced counter-menu items via curl. (1) ascendroasters.com's Shopify /products.json feed is a retail packaged-goods catalog (bagged coffee/tea for home use), not the cafe counter menu - router already flagged this. (2) Homepage links to a Heartland POS (Genius Online Ordering, mobilebytes.com backend) storefront at ascendcarlsbad.hrpos.heartland.us/menu; raw HTML is a bare React SPA shell (
, all content loaded by a bundled JS module, app-version 9.131) with zero server-rendered menu/price data. No JSON-LD, no PDF menu, no other first-party priced source found.

name: Great Wok of China
notes: Restaurant's own site (greatwokofchinaca.com) links to an order-online SPA that ships as a client-rendered Next.js shell with no server-side price data via curl. Found the same menu server-rendered with full item numbers, names and prices on two independent third-party ordering platforms: order.online/store/27717347 (305 raw $price occurrences in the SSR HTML) and beyondmenu.com (full numbered menu with descriptions). Sampled prices match exactly across both platforms (e.g. $7.58, $9.58, $11.98, $13.28, $13.68, $14.28, $14.68, $15.28, $10.58, $12.68, $12.98), which is strong cross-confirmation these are the restaurant's real posted prices rather than a platform-specific markup. A Yelp menu snippet showed a differing price for one item (Chicken Chow Mein: $12.97 vs $11.98 here) - Yelp menu data is commonly stale/cached, and is outweighed by the two matching independent sources, so filed at $11.98. Filed the full a-la-carte dinner menu (94 items, sections: Appetizers, Soup & Rice Bowls, Pork, Chicken, House Specials, Beef, Shrimp, Vegetables, Chow Mein, Fried Rice, Pan Fried Noodle) plus the 28-item Lunch Special menu (Mon-Fri 11am-3:30pm, served with soup + rice + appetizer choice per beyondmenu.com terms).

name: Masala Street San Diego - Indian Cuisine and Catering Services
notes: Restaurant's own homepage (masalastreetsandiego.com) only shows a 4-item teaser carousel with no full priced menu. The site links directly to a full-menu ordering page on iMenu4u (a third-party-hosted but first-party-linked ordering platform), which is server-rendered with complete menu/price data in raw HTML. Confirmed address on the iMenu4u page (1070 N El Camino Real Suite A, Encinitas, CA - 92024) matches the batch record exactly. Filed the complete 146-item menu across all 18 published sections (Appetizers, Signature Indian Burritos, Street Corner, Breads and Kulchas, Vegetarian, Meat Lovers, Kabab (Chefs Special), Rice Biryani, Sides & Salad, Dessert, Drinks, Combo Special, and six Catering sections). Prices follow clean printed-menu conventions (.99/.00/.50 endings), no fee-baked-in markup concerns. Note on dish names: the source site's own capitalization is inconsistent within item names (e.g. "Onion kulcha", "Bhel puri", "Papdi chaat" all have lowercase second words that are still part of the dish name), which made a reliable automated name/description split impossible without risking a fabricated wrong boundary - so each dish's full raw text (name + description as printed) was filed as the name verbatim, with description left empty, rather than guessing a split.

notes: Restaurant's own homepage (lamesapizzaworks.com) links directly to a first-party PDF menu at /assets/img/menu.pdf (2 pages, 1MB). name: Joses Pollos
notes: Batch website josespollos.com is a parked/for-sale Hostinger placeholder domain, not the real restaurant site - confirmed via curl (page is just Hostinger's parked-domain template with no restaurant content). Confirmed via Serper search that the restaurant (Jose's Pollos Estilo Acapulco, 549 25th St, San Diego, CA 92102, (619) 288-0358) is open and active on Yelp, UberEats, Grubhub, DoorDash, Postmates, Facebook, and Apple Maps, all listing the same address/phone and current hours (Tue-Sat 10am-7pm). UberEats and Yelp are bot-walled via curl (Yelp returned a DataDome CAPTCHA challenge page; UberEats 404s without a browser session) and Grubhub's default response is a client-rendered SPA shell with no server data for a normal user-agent. However, fetching the same Grubhub URL with a Googlebot user-agent string returned the fully server-side-rendered menu (Grubhub serves SSR HTML to crawlers) with complete item names, descriptions, and prices in the raw HTML (data-testid="flattened-menu-item" blocks). Extracted all 20 unique menu items this way (a 'Featured' carousel repeated 4 items also found in the full menu sections; duplicates removed). Jarritos was listed as "$3.50+" (price varies by flavor) - filed at the base $3.50 with a note in the description rather than inventing per-flavor prices.
